solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Enclosure housing a male bird

indicators.note: the enclosure word holds the next pieces inside it, as a building houses its occupants

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
HE is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A pen where a cock bird is kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a male bird' reads as one phrase describing the occupant, but the answer is the female: only 'bird' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A peahen is the female peafowl, a large pheasant-family species.

clue.text: Ward and wayward prince by court

indicators.note: wayward suggests the letters of prince stray out of line

explanation.surface: A district and an unruly prince beside a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct is a district of a town, an administrative division like an electoral ward.

clue.text: Mark has a quaintly charming way of speaking

parts.note: cute means quaintly charming
an accent is a way of speaking

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark talks with an endearing accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is the written symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute accent is a diacritical mark, as on the e of café.

clue.text: Declines, as Stanley and Beatrice lose their head

indicators.note: the couple's surname gives up its first letter

parts.note: the Webbs, Fabian socialists; the setter means Sidney and Beatrice Webb

explanation.surface: A couple's fortunes decline as they lose their wits.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous pair are Sidney and Beatrice Webb, founders of the London School of Economics; 'Stanley' is a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbs, like a falling tide, means wanes or declines.

clue.text: Offered care to wild deer

parts.note: to tend is to care for

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of deer are running loose and out of order

explanation.surface: Someone provided care for wild deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something, such as a resignation or payment, is to offer it formally.

clue.text: Record one's poems as parts of a serial

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
one's is I'S, Roman one plus 's
odes are poems

explanation.surface: Recording one's poetry as instalments of a serial.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodes are the separate instalments of a serial or series.

clue.text: Dylan dines out at theme park

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of Dylan dines are put out of order

explanation.surface: Bob Dylan eats out at an amusement park.
explanation.definitionFit: Disneyland in California is the original Disney theme park.

clue.text: Beware — danger! Contents indicated by this!

definitions.text: Beware — danger! Contents indicated by this!

indicators.note: contents says the answer is held within the words beware danger

explanation.surface: A warning label with a colour code for hazardous contents.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'bewaRE Danger', and is the colour that signals danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the colour used on warning signs to signal danger.

clue.text: Purpose of blueprint

explanation.surface: The aim of a technical plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Design covers both intent and a detailed drawing or plan.

clue.text: Sherry prize rejected — some upset

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sherry award turned down, to some dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerez de la Frontera is the Spanish town that gives sherry its name; the wine is called jerez in Spanish.

clue.text: Easy-going match has Belgium against Spain

indicators.note: the match word has the next letter held within it

parts.note: to equal is to match
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A football fixture pits Belgium against Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' simply sets E beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An equable person is calm and even-tempered, hard to ruffle.

clue.text: Fashionable teams showing guts?

parts.note: IN means in fashion
sides are teams in a game

explanation.surface: Trendy teams display courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' reads as bravery, but the answer is the literal sense, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Insides is an informal word for the stomach and bowels, the literal guts.

clue.text: High liver from Central Tibet? Wrong

indicators.note: central asks for the middle letters of Tibet, dropping its ends

parts.note: X is the cross marking an answer wrong

explanation.surface: A query whether a high-living creature comes from central Tibet, then a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High liver' suggests a bon vivant; it means an animal living high up.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat that lives on steep, high crags.

clue.text: Poor loner in obscure surroundings soon

indicators.note: in places the anagrammed loner within the obscure word
surroundings says the obscure word wraps round the jumbled letters

parts.note: to befog is to obscure

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of loner are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A miserable loner lurks in murky surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' looks like an adjective for the surroundings but is the verb; 'Poor' makes RELON, which 'in' and 'surroundings' set within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Before long is an idiom meaning shortly, in a little while.

clue.text: Arrange part for three actors in play

indicators.note: in play suggests the letters of three actors are moved about as in a game

explanation.surface: Assigning a role for three performers in a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate is to arrange music for orchestra, and by extension to organise carefully.

clue.text: Private joke, funny, but not with king — it's insulting

indicators.note: funny suggests the letters are rearranged into an odd order
the leftover letters are used without the king letter

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An in-joke is amusing, but not to a monarch, who finds it offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove K from PRIVATEJOKE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A pejorative remark is disparaging or derogatory.

clue.text: Familiar term for spaniel

definitions.meaning: ... is an informal British way of addressing a friend, as in 'me old ...'
a ... is a ... spaniel, a breed of small gun dog

explanation.surface: A colloquial word for a breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocker serves as matey slang for a pal and as the short name of a spaniel breed.

clue.text: Border security can be fatal

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
a lock provides security

explanation.surface: A warning that border security can be deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemlock is a poisonous plant whose extract kills, famously Socrates.

clue.text: Carte blanche when poor refereeing, say, is dispensed with

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in bad shape and reordered
the letters for 'say' are removed from the pool

parts.note: EG (for example) means say

explanation.surface: A referee who lets play run on gives total licence.
explanation.walkthrough: Take EG out of REFEREEING and rearrange the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Free rein means complete freedom of action, the same as carte blanche.

clue.text: Cattle crossing in this place?

parts.note: here means in this place
a ford is a river crossing

explanation.surface: Is there a cattle crossing here?
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford is a breed of red-and-white beef cattle.

clue.text: Swallows drove us wild

indicators.note: wild says the letters of drove us run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: The birds sent us into a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallows' looks like birds; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour food is to swallow it greedily.

clue.text: Small joints, we're hear, will indicate cold

indicators.note: a slip for 'we hear', signalling that the joints word is said aloud

parts.note: knees are joints

explanation.surface: Little joints, we are told, will show that someone is cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're hear' is a misprint for 'we hear', the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is a common symptom of a cold, so it signals one.

clue.text: Act violently on the French outing

parts.note: LE is the French for the
a trip is an outing

explanation.surface: Behaving badly on a French trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for acting without restraint, violently or noisily.

clue.text: In due course regret upsetting money

indicators.note: upsetting turns the pieces upward in a down entry

parts.note: so can mean 'and then, eventually'
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Eventually, remorse over losing money.
explanation.definitionFit: Euros are the currency units of the eurozone.

clue.text: Crowd actor, sadly no use and irrelevant

parts.note: an extra is an actor in a crowd scene

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters of no use are in a sorry, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A background actor is sadly useless and beside the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraneous matter is irrelevant, unrelated to the matter at hand.

clue.text: Oh, to be in France …!"

parts.note: a twist on Browning's 'Oh, to be in England': the French verb meaning 'to be'

explanation.surface: A wistful longing to be across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The line parodies Browning's poem 'Home-Thoughts, from Abroad'; read cryptically it asks for 'to be' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Être is the French infinitive for the verb 'to be'.

clue.text: "The Dog and Gander" is mentioned

indicators.note: is mentioned signals a word spoken rather than written

parts.note: a gander is a look, as is a peek

explanation.surface: A pub called The Dog and Gander comes up in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' is slang for a look, not the goose.
explanation.definitionFit: A peke is a Pekingese, a small long-haired toy dog.

clue.text: Odd characters missing from Greek work in the new adaptation

indicators.note: taking away the first, third, fifth letters and so on leaves the even letters of these words

explanation.surface: A modern version of a Greek play with some strange characters cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A rewrite is a revised version of a text, a fresh adaptation.

clue.text: Moderate Tory trebled for group

definitions.meaning: said three times it names ... ... ..., a Scottish pop band

explanation.surface: A moderate Conservative multiplied threefold for a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet labelled soft-line Tories; tripled it is the band Wet Wet Wet.

clue.text: Eoin Morgan drops most of mint chopped herb

indicators.note: the cricketer's name lets go of the next letters before the rest is rearranged
chopped says the remaining letters are cut up and reordered, as herbs are
most of drops the final letter of mint

explanation.surface: England cricket captain Eoin Morgan swaps mint for a different chopped herb.
explanation.walkthrough: MIN ('most of mint') is removed from EOINMORGAN and the rest, EOORGAN, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb of the marjoram family used in cooking.

clue.text: Designs for new transept

indicators.note: new says the letters of transept are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Plans drawn up for a new church transept.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterns are decorative designs or templates.

clue.text: Make a drastic capital cut

parts.note: a capital cut is one to the head, and capital punishment, as well as a city's budget

explanation.surface: A city council slashes its spending severely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money or a city; here it means of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead someone is to cut off the head, a capital execution.
